ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Hand Surgery Referral — Leonardo da Vinci

code.originalText: Primary care visit for weakness, numbness, and curling of the ring and little fingers of the right hand after a fall onto the elbow, with same-day brain MRI and elbow X-ray

text.paragraph: Four weeks of numbness of the ulnar fingers, weakness, and clawing of the right hand after a fall onto the bent elbow in a 65-year-old left-handed artist who paints with the right hand. Stroke has been excluded by examination and MRI. Please confirm the site and severity with nerve studies and ultrasound and advise on splinting, hand therapy, and surgery. [S]
Urgency: Soon, within two weeks; motor weakness with early wasting. [S]

list.item: Do nerve conduction studies, EMG, and ultrasound confirm ulnar neuropathy at the elbow, and do they exclude a C8 radiculopathy, plexopathy, or a lesion at the wrist?
How severe is it, and is there axonal loss?
Which splints and hand therapy do you advise, and is a corticosteroid injection useful?
Should he have surgery now or after a trial of conservative treatment, and when should that decision be made?
If surgery is needed, which procedure, and what is the place of tendon transfers for the claw?
How can he keep working, with his left hand and with adapted tools?

text.paragraph: Mr. da Vinci is a 65-year-old painter, engineer, and teacher who draws and writes with his left hand and holds the palette and does much of his brushwork with his right. Four weeks ago he slipped on stone stairs and landed on his bent right elbow; within two days the little finger and the inner half of the ring finger went numb, and the hand became weak, with curling of the ring and little fingers. He cannot hold the palette or a fine brush and drops small objects. Symptoms are worse when he leans on the elbow at his drawing table and at night. He has no neck pain and no face, speech, vision, leg, or left-hand symptoms, and the onset was not sudden. On examination there is sensory loss over the little finger, the ulnar half of the ring finger, and the dorsal ulnar hand; the first dorsal interosseous and abductor digiti minimi are 3/5 and the deep flexor of the little finger 4/5, with positive Froment and Wartenberg signs, mild clawing, and early first web wasting; thumb abduction and wrist and finger extension are normal; Tinel and elbow flexion tests are positive at the cubital tunnel. The rest of the neurological examination is normal (NIH Stroke Scale 0). Same-day MRI of the brain showed no infarct, the elbow X-ray showed no fracture, and the ECG showed sinus rhythm. Blood count, metabolic panel, HbA1c, TSH, vitamin B12, and lipids were sent. He uses a towel around the elbow at night and acetaminophen for pain. He is anxious to keep working [S]

list.item: He cannot hold the palette or a brush with his right hand and fears he will never paint again. [S]
He asks whether this is a stroke. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: A note by his grandfather Antonio records that his grandson, son of Ser Piero, was born on Saturday 15 April [1452] at the third hour of the night (Julian calendar; 24 April 1452 in the proleptic Gregorian calendar). The museums of Vinci read the note as placing his birth in Vinci itself; a long tradition places it in a farmhouse at nearby Anchiano. [D]
He was the son of Ser Piero da Vinci, a notary, and a woman named Caterina; a land-office return of 1458 lists 'Lionardo son of the said Ser Piero, not legitimate, born of him and Chaterina'. [D]

He was left-handed: the shading and hatching of his drawings slope from upper left to lower right, and his private notes, from his early twenties onward, are written in mirror script with the left hand. A review of the documents concluded that he used his right hand for work other than drawing and writing, and it has been claimed that he never painted with his left hand. [D]

The biographer Giorgio Vasari wrote that he was physically so strong that with his right hand he could bend the ring of an iron door knocker or a horseshoe as if they were lead; an engraving of about 1505 shows him playing the lira da braccio. [D]
At the invitation of King Francis I, who called him 'my father', he settled at the Château du Clos Lucé, at Amboise, in the autumn of 1516. [D]

text.paragraph: 8 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.

list.item: Weakness, numbness of the ring and little fingers, and curling of those fingers in the right hand for four weeks after a fall onto the right elbow, in a left-handed artist who uses the right hand for the palette and brushwork; stroke and a peripheral nerve lesion under evaluation: active, confirmed [S]
One fall in the past year (slipped on stone stairs and landed on the right elbow), with no loss of consciousness, dizziness, or palpitations before it; fall risk: active, confirmed [S]

Same-day assessment for stroke and localization: full neurological examination and NIH Stroke Scale, MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging, X-ray of the right elbow, and an ECG. Guideline: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome (Ulnar Nerve Entrapment at the Elbow), OrthoInfo (2026); Treatment for ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (Caliandro P, et al.) (2025); Practice parameter for electrodiagnostic studies in ulnar neuropathy at the elbow: summary statement (American Association of Electrodiagnostic Medicine, American Academy of Neurology, American Academy of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation) (1999); 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack: A Guideline From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (2021) [S]

Protect the nerve now: no leaning on the right elbow (a gel elbow pad and a padded armrest at the drawing table), avoid prolonged elbow bending, a towel loosely wrapped around the elbow at night until a splint is made; acetaminophen for pain. Guideline: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome (Ulnar Nerve Entrapment at the Elbow), OrthoInfo (2026); Treatment for ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (Caliandro P, et al.) (2025); Practice parameter for electrodiagnostic studies in ulnar neuropathy at the elbow: summary statement (American Association of Electrodiagnostic Medicine, American Academy of Neurology, American Academy of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation) (1999) [S]

Stroke risk-factor screen: blood pressure at every visit with a week of home readings, lipid panel with lipoprotein(a), HbA1c, ECG, and pulse check for atrial fibrillation. Guideline: 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack: A Guideline From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (2021); 2019 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease (2019); 2018 AHA/ACC/AACVPR/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol (2018); Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease in Adults: Preventive Medication (2022); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hyperlipidemia monograph (2026) [S]

Falls: a handrail on both sides of the stone staircase, night lighting, footwear review, and a Timed Up and Go at the wellness visit. Guideline: Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024) [S]
